target: Dedeme göre eski İstanbul çok farklıymış.
english: According to my grandfather, old Istanbul was very different.
tip: göre means according to and takes the dative: Dedeme göre, according to my grandfather, puts -e on dede.

target: Bu işi bitirirsen seni sinemaya götürürüm.
english: If you finish this task I'll take you to the cinema.
tip: bitirirsen ends in -sen, the if-you conditional: if you finish this task. The main clause then states the result.

english: Istanbul is bigger than Ankara.
tip: Turkish marks than with the ablative -dan, not a separate word: Ankara'dan daha büyük, bigger than Ankara.

english: The letter was sent yesterday.
tip: Passive adds -il to the stem: gönderdi (sent) becomes gönderildi (was sent), with no doer named.

english: I couldn't sleep because of the noise.
tip: -den dolayı means because of, and needs the ablative -den first: gürültü becomes Gürültüden dolayı (because of the noise).

english: The doctor made the patient take medicine.
tip: Causative -ir makes someone do the act: içti (drank) becomes içirdi (made take), and the taker goes dative, hastaya.

english: The student told his teacher that he didn't understand the question.
tip: To report a thought, -dığını turns the verb into a noun object: anlamadığını söyledi = said that he did not understand it.

target: Otele hava kararmadan hemen önce vardık.
english: We arrived at the hotel just before dark.
tip: -madan önce means before doing something: kararmak (to darken) becomes kararmadan önce (before it got dark).

target: Ben bu sabah şarkı söyledim çünkü sıkılmıştım.
english: I sang this morning because I was bored.
tip: -mıştım is the past before the past: sıkıldım (I got bored) becomes sıkılmıştım (I had gotten bored) for an earlier state.

target: Geçen ay trafik cezası yedim, çok kızgınım.
english: I got a traffic fine last month, I'm very angry.
tip: ceza yemek literally is to eat a fine, the normal way to say get fined: trafik cezası yedim = I got a traffic fine.

target: Komşumuz geçen hafta bahçeyle ilgilendi ve eve döndü.
english: Our neighbor took care of the garden last week and went home.
tip: ilgilenmek (to tend, take care of) pairs with -yle: bahçe becomes bahçeyle ilgilendi (took care of the garden).

english: The meals were prepared by my mother.
tip: In a passive, the doer gets tarafından (by): annem tarafından hazırlandı = were prepared by my mother.

english: When it snowed, I opened the window.
tip: -dığında means when something happened: yağmak (to fall) becomes yağdığında (when it snowed).

english: If we move to Istanbul our life changes.
tip: Proper nouns split off case suffixes with an apostrophe: İstanbul'a (to Istanbul), never written Istanbula.

english: Fill out this form and sign it.
tip: A specific, definite object takes the accusative -u: form becomes formu (the particular form) as the thing acted on.

english: I forgot to water the plants this week.
tip: unutmak takes a verb turned into a noun with -mayı: sulamak (to water) becomes sulamayı unuttum (I forgot to water).

english: If we had left earlier, we would have caught the bus.
tip: Past unreal condition: -saydık sets the if, -irdik the result: çıksaydık ... yetişirdik = had we left, we would have caught it.

target: Çok çalış ama sağlığını da ihmal etme.
english: Work hard but don't neglect your health.
tip: Written as its own word, da means also or too: sağlığını da ihmal etme = do not neglect your health either.

target: Beni dinle, sana önemli bir şey söyleyeceğim.
english: Listen to me, I'll tell you something important.
tip: sen becomes sana in the dative, an irregular form (not sene): sana ... söyleyeceğim = I will tell you.

target: Biz genellikle resim çizerdik ama yarıda bırakırdık.
english: We usually drew pictures but left them halfway.
tip: -erdik marks a repeated past habit: çizmek (to draw) becomes çizerdik (we used to draw).

english: You can come with me if you want.
tip: The -ebil in gelebilirsin adds can or able to: gel (come) plus ebil plus ir plus sin means you are able to come.

english: She has never been abroad.
tip: The -mış in çıkmamış marks hearsay: she has apparently never gone abroad, something you did not witness yourself.

english: The news was heard everywhere.
tip: The passive lives inside the verb: duy (hear) plus ul gives duyuldu, it was heard, with no doer named.

english: When the weather warmed up, I closed the door.
tip: Add -ınca to a verb for once or when: ısın (warm up) plus ınca gives ısınınca, once it warmed up.

english: I must go to the doctor, I feel very bad.
tip: The -meli in gitmeliyim means must or have to: git (go) plus meli plus yim, I must go.

target: Evet, bu konuda size katılıyorum tamamen.
english: Yes, I completely agree with you on this.
tip: katılmak (to agree with) takes the dative, so the person ends in -e: size katılıyorum, I agree with you.

target: Hava soğuk olmasına rağmen dışarı çıktık.
english: Although the weather was cold we went out.
tip: rağmen means despite and needs the dative before it: olmasına rağmen, despite its being, so despite the cold.

target: Daha dikkatli olsaydım bu hata olmazdı.
english: If I had been more careful this mistake wouldn't have happened.
tip: For an unreal past pair -saydı with -mazdı: olsaydım, had I been, plus olmazdı, would not have happened.

target: O kadar çok çalıştım ki gözlerim kapanıyor.
english: I worked so much that my eyes are closing.
tip: O kadar with ki frames a result: so much that. O kadar çalıştım ki means I worked so much that my eyes are closing.

target: Ne kadar çalışırsan çalış, mükemmel olmak zor.
english: No matter how much you work, it's hard to be perfect.
tip: Repeat the verb as aorist-conditional then bare command for no matter how: çalışırsan çalış, however much you work.
